gaps.sentence: Heavy snow made the mountain road ___ (PASS).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: impossible to travel through (im- + -able)
gaps.explanation: Heavy snow blocks the road, so the negative adjective 'impassable' (im- + pass + -able) is needed.
After 'in' a noun is needed: excitement (-ment noun).

gaps.sentence: We ___ the cost of the trip and ran out of money (ESTIMATE).
gaps.hint: judged it too low — that is why the money ran out (under-)
gaps.explanation: Running out of money shows the estimate was too low: underestimated (under- + estimated).

gaps.sentence: The ___ (INTERVIEW) asked her some difficult questions.
gaps.hint: the person who asks the questions (-er = doer)
gaps.explanation: The interviewer asks; the interviewee answers. The suffix -er marks the doer.
The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unusual. An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: The team played ___ and deserved to win (EXCELLENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'played': excellently (-ly).

gaps.sentence: The tracks become ___ after heavy rain (ACCESS).
gaps.explanation: Heavy rain blocks the tracks, so the negative adjective 'inaccessible' (in- + accessible) is needed.

gaps.sentence: She has been a loyal ___ (EMPLOY) of the firm for twenty years.
gaps.hint: person needed: someone who works for the firm
gaps.explanation: An employee works for a company; 'employment' is the uncountable state of having a job.
